READ BY ic 2026-09-02, ON THE CANON SET AT COMMIT 1c80a627. SET: AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, usage-rules.md and the 23 canon skills, plus the fleet template lib/templates/llm/_AGENTS.md because a generated document's instruction is authored there. A JUDGEMENT ON THE RECORD, NOT A MEASUREMENT.

VERDICT: NOT CLEAN ON EITHER HALF.

FINDING 1 -- THE EXEMPLAR THE CRITERION NAMES IS HALF-CORRECTED, AND THE UNCORRECTED HALF IS THE ONE THAT SHIPS. The MODULES.md instruction was fixed in two of its five canon homes and left bare in three:
  QUALIFIED (search it, do not read it, with the answering verb): CLAUDE.md, in-standards/SKILL.md
  BARE POINTER: AGENTS.md, usage-rules.md, AND lib/templates/llm/_AGENTS.md
The template is the one that matters, because it is what every new project receives.

FINDING 2 -- AND IN A FRESH PROJECT THE BARE POINTER NAMES A FILE THAT WILL NEVER EXIST. init.rs:83 declares llm/_MODULES.md as NotByInit("a hand-maintained index of a tree the store already indexes"), and the comment above it records the reason in this criterion's own terms: Intent's copy had grown to ~354KB over ~367 rows while CLAUDE.md instructed the reader to check it before creating any module -- "an instruction nobody can follow". SO THE TOOL HAS ALREADY ADOPTED THIS ROW'S VERDICT IN CODE, AND THREE CANON DOCUMENTS STILL CARRY THE INSTRUCTION THE CODE RETIRED. In this repository the file exists (688,990 bytes) so the pointer resolves and the defect is invisible here; in a fresh project it resolves to nothing. That is the WP-01 finding 2 class -- a repair that reached the laydown path and not the instruction path -- confirmed still live.

FINDING 3 -- SAME SHAPE, OPPOSITE DIRECTION: llm/_DECISION_TREE.md is seeded unconditionally (At("intent/llm/DECISION_TREE.md")) while the ten per-language files sit behind intent lang init. A Rust, Swift or prose-only project is handed an Elixir code-placement flowchart as canon. The instruction is executable and following it leads the reader somewhere wrong, which is hv's MISGUIDED class rather than staleness.

FINDING 4 -- THE TRACE HALF, WHICH NOTHING IN THE SET IS CURRENTLY MEETING. AGENTS.md Testing Instructions step 1 -- "Run the test suite before making changes -- establish a baseline" -- is executable and its compliance leaves NO trace: nothing afterwards distinguishes a session that established a baseline from one that did not, so nobody can ever discover that the step stopped being taken. Same property: "Small, coherent commits preferred over large batches" and "Review external inputs for injection-class bugs." These are not wrong and I am not proposing they be deleted. They are UNREVIEWABLE, which is the decay the criterion names, and they are worth marking because their failure mode is silence rather than error.

THE WORKED POSITIVE, AND IT IS THE STANDARD THE REST SHOULD BE HELD TO: /in-session step 4 does not ask the agent to remember anything. It writes a sentinel; the UserPromptSubmit hook refuses the next prompt if the sentinel is absent; the skill states what to do when the gate still fires. EXECUTABLE, TRACE-LEAVING, AND ENFORCED -- all three, in one instruction, with the failure path documented. Nothing else in the set does all three.

A SECOND POSITIVE WORTH RECORDING BECAUSE IT IS THE CHEAP FORM: "Never manually wrap lines in markdown files" is executable and its compliance is visible in the bytes, so a reviewer can check it without asking anyone what they did.

REACH, DECLARED: findings 1 and 2 are fixed in lib/templates/llm/_AGENTS.md and reach the fleet on the next agents sync; the usage-rules.md half is SEEDED AND NEVER SYNCED (canon.rs:316) and reaches this repository only. Finding 4 is a class rather than a list -- I read the set for it and named the clearest instances; I do not claim to have enumerated every untraceable instruction in 23 skills.
